title: check-adr-0087(runtime-export-retired): the operand names only a package's root entry, so a retired SUBPATH export (`./locales/zh` → `./locales/zh-Hans`) can only be held as no-migration-prescription
body:
domain:ui#5 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgVwQZbHRRM9CaXeKif

## What happens

`scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, category `runtime-export-retired` (#22918), reads three operand shapes: `<package>#<Export>`, `<package>#<Type>.<member>` and `<package>#*`. Predicate 1 proves the export left the package's **published root entry**. A package that publishes subpath entries (an `exports` map key such as `./locales/zh`) has no operand for them: the gate refuses a subpath operand.

## Where it showed

#30511 / PR #30595 renames `@object-ui/i18n`'s pack subpaths (`zh` → `zh-Hans`, `pt` → `pt-BR`). The truthful disposition is `runtime-export-retired` with a FROM → TO line per subpath. Because the operand cannot name a subpath, the PR holds those renames as `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` and names this gap in the marker. That is the detector-miss shape D7 set out to retire.

## Ask

Decide whether the operand grammar grows a subpath form (for example `<package>/<subpath>#<Export>` or `<package>/<subpath>#*`, predicate 1 read against that `exports` key). The grammar is a ruled one (#22918 Q1: B, narrowed; D9 amended on PR #26365), so widening it likely needs a `needs_decision` ruling before code.

Found by the #30511 card thread (os-dev-report 6664349306, out_of_scope_findings, `dedupe: adr-0087 subpath operand runtime-export-retired`).
